problem:
The position vector $r$ of a particle $P$ (relative to a fixed origin $O$) at time $t$ is given by

$$
r=⟨\frac{{3}^{t-1}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3},5t+1⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the speed of the particle at time $t=2.$
worked_solution:
First, we calculate the velocity vector $v.$ Differentiating the position vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{3}^{t-1}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5t+1)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{{3}^{t-1}\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3},5⟩ \\  & =⟨{3}^{t-1},5⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the velocity when $t=2,$ we substitute in the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(2) & =⟨{3}^{2-1},5⟩=⟨3,5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the speed at $t=2$ we calculate the magnitude of $v(2),$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|v(2)| & =\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{5}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9+25} \\  & =\sqrt{34}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the speed when $t=2$ is $\sqrt{34}.$
